::: {.home-section}
## Who the analysis helps

::: {.section-lede}
Pharmacies decide neither prescriptions, prices nor supply, yet bear the results. This work starts from pharmacy problems and uses public data to build evidence for those who could ease them with ordering, stock and return information.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="audience">
  <div><h3>Pharmacies</h3><p>Know in advance when and how much prices will be cut, and which ingredients' demand swings.</p></div>
  <div><h3>Distributors</h3><p>Use price-cut alerts and ingredient demand baselines for pharmacy alerts and supply planning.</p></div>
  <div><h3>Pharmacy support services</h3><p>Combine them with a pharmacy's order and stock records to decide what to check and what to watch.</p></div>
  <div><h3>Also useful for</h3><p>Drug makers and prescribers can check ingredient markets and reimbursement changes on the same evidence.</p></div>
</div>
```
:::

::: {.home-section}
## How I work

::: {.principle}
Find the action with the least resistance that can still be carried out within the constraints.
:::

If there is no evidence that a complex method beats a simple one, I choose the simple one. I fix decision rules before seeing results, and I report unfavorable results as they are.
:::
